summary: A live Ausca Browser Session was discovered from the current catalog, challenged over x402 v2, paid with 0.05 USDC on Base, connected through standard CDP, used to load a public page and read its title, then explicitly closed and independently verified closed.

observations.result: Fetched the live catalog and confirmed offer browser.session, revision browser-duration-r3, exact schema digests, POST /v1/lease-browser, and the 600-second price of 5 USD cents.
The unchanged invocation envelope returned HTTP 402 with x402Version 2, amount 50000 atomic USDC units, network eip155:8453, and payTo 0x26572ff23c6c52bfb1a69cb0c9114a8be443b422.

The same request bytes and idempotency key were retried with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. The x402 settlement succeeded for 0.05 USDC in Base transaction 0x3eef40a5815bf8b453c6b1d1f7757d5dcef253568a299686a09df06981d3bc44.

The paid POST returned HTTP 200 with status accepted. Invocation paid_1e226da9-37ca-480e-903e-038580e2a662 was already succeeded and output digest sha256:7463577600b8a76a11243e8caeb51e838e1bac8d1e37148a9dcaed22e3b81ae1 identified a ready ten-minute lease.
No terminal polling was required because the paid response already reported invocation state succeeded. A later public invocation read was used to obtain and validate the receipt reference.
Authenticated GET /v1/browser-sessions/{session_id} returned HTTP 200 and authoritative session state ready with the expected creation and hard-expiry timestamps.

POST /v1/browser-sessions/{session_id}/connections with Idempotency-Key ajp-gofrantic-134-cdp-v1 returned HTTP 200 and one short-lived WSS ticket. The URL and lease capability were not retained in public evidence.
Connected with CDP protocol 1.3 to Chrome/128.0.6613.137, created a target, navigated to https://example.com/, and evaluated document.title as Example Domain.

Validated the exact offer revision and schema bindings, succeeded invocation state, output digest, session identity, loaded URL, returned page title, and lifecycle timestamps against the live responses.

GET of the public RunX receipt returned HTTP 200 and named Ausca Browser Session as completed. The initial succeeded paid response did not include receipt_ref, so GET /v1/invocations/paid_1e226da9-37ca-480e-903e-038580e2a662 was required to obtain it.
DELETE /v1/browser-sessions/{session_id} returned HTTP 200, status closed, state closed, and closed_at 2026-09-19T07:31:51.959Z.
A separate authenticated status read after deletion returned HTTP 200 with the same session id, state closed, and the same closed_at timestamp.
Total elapsed from the paid request start through independently verified closure was 66.342 seconds.

issues.issue: The HTTP 200 body reported invocation.state=succeeded but omitted invocation.receipt_ref. The caller had to discover that GET /v1/invocations/paid_1e226da9-37ca-480e-903e-038580e2a662 would return the receipt later.

The lifecycle prose says the connection request returns a WebSocket URL, but does not show that the field is nested at connection.websocket_url. A first strict parser expected websocket_url at the top level and had to recover with the same idempotency key.

The public receipt page identified Ausca Browser Session and completion, but the rendered page did not expose the 0.05 USD amount or exact offer bindings needed for a human to verify the bounty without consulting the invocation and evidence packet.

After an acknowledged close, the public invocation output remains the creation-time resource_lease state ready. Only the capability-protected browser-session status reflects state closed, so lifecycle truth is split across two surfaces.

proposed_change: Add a complete Browser Session response example showing connection.websocket_url, document the receipt readback when a succeeded admission omits receipt_ref, and expose a redacted terminal lifecycle state alongside the public invocation so operators can verify closure without lease authority.
